# API reference

The package documentation, as `go doc -all` prints it. The same text is on
[pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/veggiemonk/workflow).

```
package workflow // import "github.com/veggiemonk/workflow"

Package workflow composes typed units of work into a pipeline.

# The Step value

Step is a concrete generic struct, not an interface. A step declares its own
input type and its own output type:

    Step[I, O any]  // Run(ctx, I) (O, error)

A struct is necessary because Go 1.27 allows type parameters on a method only
when the receiver is a concrete type. An interface method must have no type
parameters. Generic methods are what let a chain change its type:

    parse := workflow.Func("Parse", func(ctx context.Context, s string) (Tokens, error) { ... })
    count := workflow.Func("Count", func(ctx context.Context, t Tokens) (int, error) { ... })
    pipeline := parse.Then(count) // Step[string, int]

To write a step on a type that carries state, implement Runner and wrap it with
Of. Runner is a plain interface, so it stays legal.

# A step is immutable

Every method returns a new Step. No method writes to its receiver. A step is
therefore safe to share, to reuse and to run concurrently. Middleware is applied
once, when the step is built, never while it runs.

# Concurrency

Step.Par runs two steps on the same input and joins their results with a
function you supply. Fan does the same for any number of steps that share an
output type. Each applies one step to every element of a slice. All three keep
the results typed, so no result can be lost, and none of them copies your data.

# Errors

A concurrent combinator collects every branch error with errors.Join. It does
not stop at the first one.

VARIABLES

var ErrCircuitOpen = errors.New("workflow: circuit breaker is open")
    ErrCircuitOpen is returned while a CircuitBreaker is open.

var ErrNilStep = errors.New("workflow: step holds no function")
    ErrNilStep is returned when a zero Step is run. A zero Step holds no
    function. Build every step with Func, Of or Pure.


FUNCTIONS

func StepID(ctx context.Context) (string, bool)
    StepID returns the identifier that Step.WithID put in the context.


TYPES

type CircuitBreaker struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    CircuitBreaker stops calling a step that keeps failing.

    The breaker is an explicit value, so you decide what shares it. Give one
    breaker to one step to guard that step alone. Give the same breaker to
    several steps only when they all depend on the same remote service.

func NewCircuitBreaker(cfg CircuitBreakerConfig) *CircuitBreaker
    NewCircuitBreaker builds a breaker.

type CircuitBreakerConfig struct {
	// FailureThreshold is the count of failures in a row that opens the
	// circuit. Below 1 means 5.
	FailureThreshold int
	// OpenTimeout is how long the circuit stays open. Below 1 means 60s.
	OpenTimeout time.Duration
	// ShouldTrip decides whether an error counts as a failure.
	// A nil ShouldTrip counts every error.
	ShouldTrip func(error) bool
}
    CircuitBreakerConfig configures a CircuitBreaker.

type Middleware[I, O any] func(Step[I, O]) Step[I, O]
    Middleware wraps a step to add behaviour such as logging or retry.

    Middleware is applied once, when you build the step. Step.Use returns a new
    step and leaves the receiver unchanged, so a step can never collect a second
    layer of middleware when you run it again.

type PanicError struct {
	Step  string
	Value any
	Stack []byte
}
    PanicError reports a panic that a step raised. Every concurrent combinator
    turns a panic into a PanicError, so a panic in one branch never leaves a
    zero result behind and never crashes the program.

func (e *PanicError) Error() string

type RetryConfig struct {
	// MaxAttempts counts the first try as well. Below 1 means 3.
	MaxAttempts int
	// InitialDelay is the wait before the first retry. Below 1 means 100ms.
	InitialDelay time.Duration
	// MaxDelay caps the wait. Below 1 means 5s.
	MaxDelay time.Duration
	// BackoffMultiplier multiplies the wait after each try. Below 1 means 2.
	BackoffMultiplier float64
	// ShouldRetry decides whether an error is worth another try.
	// A nil ShouldRetry retries every error.
	ShouldRetry func(error) bool
}
    RetryConfig configures Step.Retry.

type Runner[I, O any] interface {
	Run(context.Context, I) (O, error)
}
    Runner is the extension point for a type that carries state.

    Its method has no type parameters, which an interface method may not have,
    so any type may implement it. Wrap an implementation with Of to get a
    composable Step.

type Step[I, O any] struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Step is one unit of work. It reads an I and returns an O.

    Step is a value. Every method returns a new Step and leaves the receiver
    unchanged, so a Step is safe to share and to run more than once.

    The zero Step is not usable; it returns ErrNilStep.

func Each[I, O any](concurrency int, s Step[I, O]) Step[[]I, []O]
    Each applies s to every element of a slice, at most concurrency at a time.
    Give a concurrency of 0 or less to run every element at the same time.

    Each cannot be a method. A method that returns Step[[]I, []O] would make the
    compiler instantiate Step[[][]I, [][]O], and so on without end. The compiler
    rejects that as an instantiation cycle.

func Fan[I, O, R any](name string, join func([]O) (R, error), steps ...Step[I, O]) Step[I, R]
    Fan runs every step on the same input at the same time, then joins the
    results, in the order the steps were given, with join.

    Every step must share the same output type. Use Step.Par when the outputs
    differ. Every step runs to completion; Fan joins every error.

func Func[I, O any](name string, f func(context.Context, I) (O, error)) Step[I, O]
    Func builds a step from a function.

func Identity[T any]() Step[T, T]
    Identity returns a step that returns its input unchanged.

func If[I, O any](name string, pred func(context.Context, I) bool, then, els Step[I, O]) Step[I, O]
    If runs then when pred returns true, and els when it returns false.

func Of[I, O any](name string, r Runner[I, O]) Step[I, O]
    Of builds a step from a Runner.

func Pure[I, O any](name string, f func(I) O) Step[I, O]
    Pure builds a step from a function that cannot fail.

func Seq[T any](name string, steps ...Step[T, T]) Step[T, T]
    Seq chains steps that share one type. It is Step.Then for the common case
    where the type does not change.

func (s Step[I, O]) Breaker(cb *CircuitBreaker) Step[I, O]
    Breaker blocks the step while cb is open.

func (s Step[I, O]) Log(l *slog.Logger) Step[I, O]
    Log records the name, the duration and the error of each run.

    Log never records the input or the output. A payload can hold a secret,
    and formatting it costs more than the step itself in a hot pipeline.

func (s Step[I, O]) Map[P any](name string, f func(O) (P, error)) Step[I, P]
    Map returns a step that runs s, then applies f to its output. It is
    Step.Then for a plain function.

func (s Step[I, O]) Name() string
    Name returns the name of the step.

func (s Step[I, O]) Par[B, R any](other Step[I, B], join func(O, B) (R, error)) Step[I, R]
    Par runs s and other on the same input at the same time, then joins their
    results with join.

    The join is typed, so the compiler will not let a result be dropped. Neither
    branch receives a copy of the input: give Par steps that do not write to it.

    Both branches always run to completion. If both fail, Par returns both
    errors joined with errors.Join.

func (s Step[I, O]) Recover() Step[I, O]
    Recover turns a panic raised by the step into a PanicError.

    [Par], Fan and Each already do this for every branch, because a panic in
    a goroutine stops the program. A step that runs in sequence does not need
    Recover: its panic travels up the caller's own stack, as Go intends.

func (s Step[I, O]) Rename(name string) Step[I, O]
    Rename returns a copy of the step with a new name.

func (s Step[I, O]) Retry(cfg RetryConfig) Step[I, O]
    Retry runs the step again when it fails, with exponential backoff. It stops
    early when the context ends.

func (s Step[I, O]) Run(ctx context.Context, in I) (O, error)
    Run executes the step.

    Run checks the context before it starts. It returns the zero O on error.

func (s Step[I, O]) String() string
    String prints the step and its children as a tree.

func (s Step[I, O]) Then[P any](next Step[O, P]) Step[I, P]
    Then returns a step that runs s, then feeds its output to next.

    P is a type parameter of the method, so the chain may change type at every
    link. Go infers P from next.

        parse.Then(count).Then(format) // Step[Doc, string]

func (s Step[I, O]) Timeout(d time.Duration) Step[I, O]
    Timeout gives the step a context with a deadline.

    The step must honour the context. Timeout does not start a goroutine and
    it does not abandon a running step, because Go cannot stop a goroutine from
    outside. A step that does no I/O must test ctx.Err() itself.

func (s Step[I, O]) Use(mw ...Middleware[I, O]) Step[I, O]
    Use applies middleware to the step and returns the wrapped step. The first
    middleware given is the outermost.

func (s Step[I, O]) WithID() Step[I, O]
    WithID puts a fresh UUID in the context for the length of the run. Read it
    with StepID.
```
